tasks.title: signal option does not reject when task is aborted while queued
Per-task `timeout` in `add()` skips validation that the constructor enforces
tasks.body:
## Bug

The constructor validates the global `timeout` option and throws a clear `TypeError` for non-positive values. But `add()` accepts per-task `timeout` without any equivalent check.

This leads to two silent failure modes:

**Case 1 — `timeout: 0` silently disables the global timeout**

The guard inside `add()` is:

\`\`\`ts
if (options.timeout) {
  operation = pTimeout(Promise.resolve(operation), { milliseconds: options.timeout, ... });
}
\`\`\`

`if (0)` is falsy, so `timeout: 0` bypasses the wrapping entirely. If a queue was constructed with `timeout: 5000`, passing `{ timeout: 0 }` to a specific task silently drops the timeout for that task. There's no error and no documentation of this escape hatch.

**Case 2 — `timeout: -1` produces a cryptic internal error**

`p-timeout` validates its `milliseconds` argument and throws synchronously when it's not strictly positive. That TypeError propagates out of `add()` as an unhandled rejection — but the message names `p-timeout` internals, not the `add()` call-site, making it hard to trace.

## Expected

Both cases should throw a clear `TypeError` at the `add()` call-site, consistent with the constructor:

\`\`\`
TypeError: Expected `timeout` to be a positive finite number, got `0`
\`\`\`

tasks.title: `onDownloadProgress` never emits `percent: 1` for empty response bodies
tasks.body:
### Summary

When a response has an empty body (for example a `200` with `Content-Length: 0`), `onDownloadProgress` never fires with `percent: 1`. The documented guarantee is that `onDownloadProgress` always reports completion, but for empty bodies the final event is skipped.

tasks.title: Bug: `replaceOption` and `undefined` do not work with `signal` option in `ky.extend()`
pAll incorrectly infers type to unknown[] when pAll has nested promises (unless the function is async)
Incorrect typings for index.d.mts
tasks.body:
I was just updating some dependencies of some of my projects and noticed I was getting a new error with the latest eventemitter3 release.

`EventEmitter' cannot be used as a value because it was imported using 'import type'.`

The [index.d.mts](https://github.com/primus/eventemitter3/blob/master/index.d.mts) file seems to be re-exporting only the type of the EventEmitter class, so TypeScript will not treat it as a value that can be instantiated.
